Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass control matrix (redwood_admin_control_matrix_v1.xlsx) and answering inline below. Happy to set up a 30-minute call if your GRC needs to walk through specifics.

Quick answers:
- Admin roles: Redwood supports multi-level admin roles. Tenant Admin (full), Org Admin (scoped), Support Admin (read/troubleshoot), and Audit-Only. Roles can be scoped to a subset of tenant resources via resource tags; we'll include examples in the matrix.
- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 with PATCH (delta) and bulk provisioning. Group writeback to Okta is not provided out-of-the-box (we can provide webhook hooks you can use), but group-to-role mapping is configurable in the Console and via APIs.
- SSO attributes: We accept both SAML and OIDC assertions. Preferred flow is to use IDP groups for session-time attributes and SCIM for persistent assignments when you need authoritative group membership. Example mappings included in the matrix.

2) If you want, Marissa can run a short technical workshop with your IAM owner to validate mappings and run a test SCIM sync.

Hi Elaine / IT-Ops team — looping in more technical details below and an example SCIM mapping snippet you can share with your IdP team. I’ll also note our best-practice recommendation.

Best-practice: Use SCIM as the source of truth for long-lived role assignments (e.g., project-level access, billing admins) and use IDP group claims for session-specific elevated capabilities. This avoids clock-skew and transient-sync issues during deployments.

SCIM behavior:
- Protocol: SCIM 2.0 (RFC7644) 
- Provisioning types: POST for create, PUT for replace, PATCH for delta updates, DELETE for remove
- Group writeback: Not native. We emit audit webhooks for membership changes; customers often configure Okta Workflows or Azure Logic Apps to reconcile.

Example mapping (SCIM group -> Redwood role):
- scim_group.displayName = "ops-redwood-admins" -> role: "Org Admin" (scoped to resource-tag:ops)
- scim_group.displayName = "redwood-audit" -> role: "Audit-Only" (read-only)

SCIM PATCH sample (group membership add):
PATCH /Groups/{id}
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "add",
      "path": "members",
      "value": [ { "value": "248289e3-08b4-407b-8f54-1a3f0b2a0d1c", "display": "j.smith@lighthousecap.com" } ]
    }
  ]
}

We will provide a JSON example for SAML attribute mapping (SAML nameID / attributes -> redwood:email, redwood:externalId, redwood:groups). Marissa will coordinate the test window if you provide an SP-initiated SAML metadata or OIDC client info.

Hi Elaine / IT-Ops — adding some technical guarantees and operational notes from the platform side.

1) RBAC primitives and enforcement:
- Roles: Tenant Admin, Org Admin, Support Admin, Billing Admin, Audit-Only.
- Policy scoping: Roles can be scoped to resource tags, model groups, or project IDs. Enforcement is enforced at the API gateway layer and the serving runtime via short-lived access tokens.
- Admin impersonation: Support Admins can impersonate non-admin users for troubleshooting but cannot escalate privileges. All impersonation events are logged.

2) SCIM specifics and performance SLAs:
- SCIM API rate limits: default 120 requests/minute with burst allowed; rate limits are configurable for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Delta sync reliability: PATCH and incremental syncs are idempotent; we persist a server-side sync cursor per tenant to resume after interruptions.

3) SSO attribute handling (SAML/OIDC):
- We support both SAML assertions and OIDC ID tokens for session mapping.
- Attribute precedence: if an authenticated session contains groups claim, those groups are applied as session claims. Persistent group membership is authoritative from SCIM unless tenant config sets IDP as authoritative.

4) Audit and evidentiary controls:
- Admin operations audit trail: retained 2 years by default (configurable up to 7 years on enterprise plans).
- Privileged access logs include actor, target resource, action, timestamp, source IP, user agent, and request payload hash.
- For session recordings / console activity: we capture command-level metadata and can export session transcripts on request (no full keystroke capture).

5) Emergency access / break-glass process:
- Support for MFA-protected, time-limited emergency access tokens. Requests generate an automatic ticket and require two approvers for activation (can be mapped to Lighthouse's approver list).

If useful, Ben can help with a short runbook that maps Lighthouse's required control IDs to the fields in the attached matrix.

Thanks,
